key_insight: An agentic, stateful AI workbench—the AI Co-Mathematician—augments mathematicians across ideation, literature search, computation, theorem proving, and theory building, while explicitly managing uncertainty and tracking failed hypotheses to support open-ended research.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between static AI tools and the iterative, exploratory nature of mathematical research by providing an asynchronous, intent-refining workspace that preserves state, provenance, and failed lines of inquiry.
method: Orchestrates specialized AI agents (ideation, search, symbolic computation, prover) within a single, asynchronous stateful workspace.
Manages uncertainty and refines user intent by recording provenance, tracking failed hypotheses, and enabling iterative exploration and hypothesis reactivation.
Integrates literature search, computational experiments, and theorem-proving workflows to support end-to-end theory development and reproducible research artifacts.
impact: Demonstrates how agentic, stateful AI systems can materially accelerate complex research workflows, improving productivity, reproducibility, and collaboration for AI/ML practitioners and domain scientists; serves as a model for similar workbenches in other scientific fields.
visual_elements: Workspace overview diagram showing multiple agent types (ideation, search, compute, prover) connected to a central state store with provenance links
Pipeline flowchart illustrating a typical loop: idea → literature search → computational experiment → proof attempt → record outcome (success/failure)
Before/after chart or icon set quantifying workflow benefits (time saved, hypotheses tracked, reproducibility gains)
Example interaction snapshot: staged dialogue and state history showing a failed hypothesis being refined and re-tested
paper_title: AI Co-Mathematician: Accelerating Mathematicians with Agentic AI
paper_authors: Daniel Zheng, Ingrid von Glehn, Yori Zwols, Iuliya Beloshapka, Lars Buesing
